title: Frontend mid domain memoization rerenders
question: In a framework like React, what actually causes a component to re-render, and how do memoization tools help, and how can they backfire?
idealAnswer:
A component re-renders when its own state changes, when its parent re-renders (by default, children re-render too, regardless of whether their props changed), or when context it consumes changes

React.memo (or equivalent) skips re-rendering a component if its props are shallow-equal to the previous render, this only helps if the parent would otherwise re-render it unnecessarily

useMemo caches an expensive computed value between renders, and useCallback caches a function reference, both exist mainly to keep referential equality stable so memoized children (or dependency arrays) don't invalidate unnecessarily

Overusing memoization has real costs: added code complexity, memory to store cached values, and the comparison itself has a cost, memoizing a cheap computation can be net slower than just recomputing it

A common mistake is memoizing a component but still passing it a new inline object, array, or function as a prop each render, which breaks the shallow-equality check and defeats the memoization entirely

Profiling (e.g. React DevTools Profiler) should drive where memoization is applied, rather than applying it reflexively everywhere
